exposure: Modified embedded vertical mattress suture technique combined with trapezoidal resection
Traditional subcutaneous fat layer discontinuous suture
outcome: Postoperative scar formation (grade A healing rate, hypertrophic scar incidence, VSS score, scar width)
cohort: 339 pregnant women who underwent cesarean sections at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, the First Affiliated Hospital of Xiamen University.
finding: Trapezoidal resection combined with improved buried vertical mattress suture technique significantly promoted incision healing, reduced suture reaction, incision pain, adverse complications, and hypertrophic scar incidence, while also improving the cosmetic effect compared to traditional suture methods.
mod_finding: The application of trapezoidal resection combined with improved buried vertical mattress suture technique during cesarean section significantly enhanced incision healing, reduced adverse complications and hypertrophic scar formation, and improved cosmetic satisfaction.
